curriculum.lesson_evidence: A fitness challenge circuit builds strength, stamina and flexibility using stations such as step-ups, wall push-ups, chair squats, skipping and stretching. Warm up first, work at your own pace for 30 to 40 seconds per station, rest briefly and cool down with gentle stretches. Challenge yourself, not others, by comparing with your own earlier results. Stop if you feel pain or dizziness and keep water close.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A circuit has no warm-up and no water break. Write one change for each and say why.

FEEDBACK
Add 2 minutes of marching and arm circles first to prepare the muscles, and a water break after each round to replace fluid. Warm-ups help prevent injury and water breaks keep the body safe.

WATCH FOR
Believing you should push through pain. Stop if anything hurts or you feel unwell; feeling puffed from effort is different from pain.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Design a five-station fitness circuit using household items, with a warm-up, a cool-down, timings and easier and harder choices. Do it with family, record your counts at each station, repeat in a week and compare with your own results. Stop if you feel unwell.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example circuit. 1 Step-ups on a low step. 2 Wall push-ups. 3 Chair squats (sit down to a chair and stand up). 4 Skipping. 5 Balance on one foot. 30 seconds each, 15 seconds rest. Warm-up: march on the spot for 2 minutes. Cool-down: gentle arm and leg stretches. Sara records 12 chair squats, then 15 the next week.

TRY FIRST
A circuit has no warm-up and no water break. Write one change for each and say why.

FEEDBACK
Add 2 minutes of marching and arm circles first to prepare the muscles, and a water break after each round to replace fluid. Warm-ups help prevent injury and water breaks keep the body safe.
teach_steps.explain:
A fitness challenge circuit builds strength, stamina and flexibility using stations such as step-ups, wall push-ups, chair squats, skipping and stretching. Warm up first, work at your own pace for 30 to 40 seconds per station, rest briefly and cool down with gentle stretches. Challenge yourself, not others, by comparing with your own earlier results. Stop if you feel pain or dizziness and keep water close.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the cues, rules or choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For any movement, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby, move at your own comfortable level and stop if anything hurts or feels unsafe. You may always choose a gentler version or only describe the movement. One deliberate, reasoned change is more useful than a longer answer.

Warm up first, work at your own pace for 30 to 40 seconds per station, rest briefly and cool down with gentle stretches. Challenge yourself, not others, by comparing with your own earlier results. Stop if you feel pain or dizziness and keep water close. Now choose a different situation to show you can transfer the idea.
teaching.rule: Use the same PDHPE idea in a new place, game or situation, not a copy of the example. Review safety, fairness and inclusion.
teaching.why: This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.
